nonce.semantic: nonce applied to inline <style> and <script> tags rendered by Base UI components; must match the CSP header nonce

disableStyleElements.semantic: stop rendering inline <style> elements; you must then supply the CSS yourself (e.g. .base-ui-disable-scrollbar { scrollbar-width: none } + ::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none })

children.semantic: wrap the app or a subtree

renderProp: Not applicable — CSPProvider takes children only and renders no element of its own; it is a context provider. Export shape is a plain named export (`import { CSPProvider } from '@base-ui/react/csp-provider'`), NOT a namespace object.
controlled: Not applicable — no state, no open/close, no callbacks.
notableDifferences: No React Aria counterpart: this exists purely to satisfy strict CSPs by nonce-ing Base UI's inline <style>/<script> tags.

Affects only inline <style>/<script> ELEMENTS, never inline style attributes (style-src-attr is out of scope) — components that rely on inline styles (e.g. ScrollArea.Viewport, Select.Popup/List when alignItemWithTrigger is on) may need 'unsafe-inline', client-only rendering, or manually unset inline styles.
`<script>` tags are opt-in and have no disable flag, so a nonce is still required when any component uses inline scripts.
Exact export surface (verified in csp-provider/index.d.ts): `export { CSPProvider } from './index.parts.js'; export type * from './CSPProvider.js'` — there is no `CSPProvider.Provider` alias.
